reviewer: Captain (implementation finding; not a counsel approval)
question: What is caseMode for the two filed components of the Oregon set-aside-without-conviction specification: is the motion filed into an existing criminal case, or does it open a new one?
finding: Neither, universally. This route spans both situations, and the repository's own identifiers disagree about which one it is because each is describing a different half of it.

sources.controlling: "Where no accusatory instrument is filed, at any time after 60 days from the date the prosecuting attorney indicates that the state has elected not to proceed ... an arrested, cited or charged person may apply to the court in the county in which the person was arrested, cited or charged for an order setting aside the record of the arrest, citation or charge."

theTwoSituations.precondition: no accusatory instrument was ever filed
theTwoSituations.consequence: there is no criminal case to file into; the person applies to the circuit court of the county of arrest
theTwoSituations.timing: 60 days from the prosecuting attorney's declination

theTwoSituations.precondition: an accusatory instrument was filed and the charge was dismissed
theTwoSituations.consequence: the case exists; the motion and proposed order go into it

theTwoSituations.precondition: an accusatory instrument was filed and tried to acquittal
theTwoSituations.consequence: the case exists; the motion and proposed order go into it

evidence.whyTheGeneratorCouldNotDecide: All three branches share one venue sentence — "the circuit court of the county in which the person was arrested, cited or charged" — because it fixes the COUNTY, not which case. The contract generator reads the recorded filing action, and that sentence is silent on case mode, so it correctly recorded unresolved rather than guessing.

theIdentifierConflict.routeKeyAndPathwayId: set-aside-of-arrests-or-charges-without-conviction-under-ors-137-225-1-c — names the (1)(c) branch, which is the no-accusatory-instrument situation, i.e. new_case
theIdentifierConflict.manifestTrackId: or_acquittal — an acquittal presupposes a filed accusatory instrument, i.e. existing_case
theIdentifierConflict.routeLabel: "arrests OR charges without conviction" — spans both on its face
theIdentifierConflict.reading: The identifiers are not in error about the law; they are each naming one side of a route that covers both. Resolving the disagreement by preferring one identifier would silently drop the other situation.

routeShapeDetermination.question: Are the no-instrument matters and the acquittal matters one procedural and document family whose only difference is caseMode, or do they need separate route and document treatment?
routeShapeDetermination.answer: Separate treatment. They are not one family, and a conditional caseMode would hide a wrong route model rather than express a real one.

comparedFromMemo.or_arrest_no_charges: Motion to Set Aside the Record of an Arrest, Citation or Charge Where No Accusatory Instrument Was Filed
comparedFromMemo.or_dismissed_charge: Motion to Set Aside the Record of a Dismissed Charge
comparedFromMemo.or_acquittal: Motion to Set Aside the Record After an Acquittal

comparedFromMemo.or_arrest_no_charges: the office of the prosecuting attorney who HAD AUTHORITY TO PROSECUTE — there being no prosecution
comparedFromMemo.or_dismissed_charge: the office of the prosecuting attorney who PROSECUTED the charge
comparedFromMemo.or_acquittal: the office of the prosecuting attorney who PROSECUTED the charge

comparedFromMemo.or_arrest_no_charges: 60 days from the prosecuting attorney's declination
Oregon circuit court for the county of arrest, citation or charge

routeShapeDetermination.consequence: One runtime route is currently standing in for two different statutory subsections. Its routeKey and pathwayId name 137.225(1)(c); its packet-set trackId names or_acquittal, which is a (1)(d) branch. That is the visible symptom of the wrong route model, not a naming slip.

caseModeOnceSplit.or_arrest_no_charges: new_case — no accusatory instrument was filed, so there is no case to file into

decision: Split the route in §5 rather than assigning a single caseMode or a conditional one. The legal basis, the named vehicle, the service recipient and the timing precondition all differ between the (1)(c) no-instrument branch and the two (1)(d) branches; only the filing destination is shared. Once split, caseMode resolves per branch from the branch's own authority and needs no conditional and no new packet fact. Until then caseMode stays unresolved on or_acquittal-primary-filing-1 and or_acquittal-proposed-order-2 and both components stay non-releaseable.
implementation: Route-productization work in §5: give each of the three memo branches its own route, vehicle and component set, carry each through registry, state pack, planner, renderer selection, fixtures and acceptance, and then state caseMode per branch. Do NOT add an 'Was an accusatory instrument filed?' question to the frozen screening flow to keep one route: the branches are already distinguishable by the disposition the participant has answered, and a conditional would be a route-model defect wearing a packet fact.
notModelledHere: Which of the three branches the existing or_acquittal-set packet and its OJD form set were actually drafted against, and whether the OR-OJD-ADULT-SET-ASIDE-PACKET form covers all three. That is the first question the §5 split has to answer from the form itself.
supersedesOnly: The implicit expectation that every filed component resolves to one of existing_case or new_case. Other jurisdictions are unchanged.
remainingReview: The specification already records legalSectionsBound: false, so it composes nothing and sells nothing today. Counsel review of the branch split, the exact intake question that establishes whether an accusatory instrument was filed, and the 60-day declination timing on the uncharged branch all remain required.
